previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with fevers, cough, and shortness of breath found to be due to a new left lower lobe pneumonia. He had brown sputum and worsening dyspnea, with a history of COPD and multiple myeloma. He was treated with IV Cefepime, Vancomycin, and Levofloxacin, with improvement in symptoms and sputum clearance. His COPD was managed with continued Symbicort and Spiriva, and he remained off supplemental oxygen. His Warfarin dose was adjusted due to a high INR of 3.7 interacting with Levofloxacin; he was instructed to hold Warfarin on discharge day, take 5 mg the next day, and follow up with the anticoagulation clinic. He was discharged home on oral Levofloxacin for a full 14-day course, with stable mental status and baseline breathing. Follow-up was arranged with his primary and specialty providers.

Brief Hospital Course:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN:  ___ year old male with a pmh sig for 
multiple medical problems, including multiple myeloma for which 
he is currently undergoing chemo, a-fib, HTN, CHF, CAD, COPD, 
admitted with a new LLL pneumonia.
.  
.  
#  Pneumonia: Found to have LLL pneumonia on radiograph. He was 
started on levofloxacin in the clinic and he had been given 1L 
NS in the office as well. He is mildly short of breath though 
remained afebrile throughout admission. He was transiently 
switched to Cefepime after arrival to the floor because he 
became confused and there was concern for worsening pneumonia. 
An ABG was done, and it showed PO2 of 66 and sat of 88. He was 
started on oxygen at the time (2L NC). He improved over the 
weekend, and was switched back to levofloxacin. His AMS resolved 
(see below). On ___ his ambulatory sat was 90% and 
his heart rate doubled to 115 from 58. We checked a chest x-ray 
showing worsening pneumonia - ___ was consulted on ___, 
failed a bronch due to agitation. A chest CT showed LLL 
pneumonia. He was started on Cefepime and Vanc on ___, and 
improved until time of discharge. Fungal infection was 
considered but his clinical improvement on IV antibiotics made 
it less likely. He was sent home with services to complete a 14 
day course of IV antibiotics. A prescription of outpatient labs 
was sent with the ___ with results to be sent to Dr. ___ 
___ until ___ on ___.
.
#  ARF: New bump in creatinine, likely in the setting of 
dehydration and pre-renal azotemia, however it may be as a 
result of his MM. He was bolused 1L of fluid in the clinic. He 
was transfused a unit of blood and given another liter of fluid 
and his creatinine trended down. It improved to 1.3 at best, and 
was 1.6 on time of discharge. Initial urine culture grew 
enterococcus and was treated with ampicillin.
.  
#  Tachycardia: He has a history of a-fib, and he is currently 
being anticoagulated on warfarin. His tachycardia responded to 
fluid resuscitation and he remained in atrial flutter at a rate 
of approximately 60 BPMs for the remainder of his 
hospitaliztion.
.
#  Coagulopathy: He was admitted with a supratherapeutic INR of 
4.1, and peaked at 5.7 he was reversed with vitamin K and FFP. 
He was restarted on 2mg of coumadin and his INR at time of 
discharge was 1.9.
.  
#  Multiple Myeloma: He was currently undergoing treatment with 
Decadron, Cytoxan, and Revlamid. A new cycle was started and he 
was given a dose of Cytoxan in the hospital. He was discharged 
with 3 days of neupogen for decreasing counts and transfused an 
additional unit of blood for a HCT of 25.  He was sent home with 
___ for lab checks and IV antibiotics.

MRI OF THE HEAD.

CLINICAL INDICATION:  ___ man with PMH of MM, admitted for pneumonia
which is improving, now with altered mental status changes, evaluate for
intracranial mass lesion or other intracranial process.

COMPARISON:  Prior CT of the head dated ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Sagittal T1, axial T2, axial FLAIR, axial magnetic susceptibility
and axial diffusion-weighted sequences were obtained.

FINDINGS:  There is no evidence of acute intracranial hemorrhage, mass, mass
effect or shifting of the normally midline structures.  The T2 and FLAIR
sequences, demonstrate few scattered foci of high signal intensity,
distributed in the periventricular white matter, which are nonspecific and may
represent microvascular ischemic disease.  Normal flow void signal is
identified at the major vascular structures.  No diffusion abnormalities are
detected to suggest acute or subacute ischemic changes.  The orbits are
unremarkable, the paranasal sinuses demonstrate opacity of the left maxillary
sinus with mucosal thickening, unchanged since the prior head CT dated
___.

IMPRESSION:
1.  There is no evidence of acute intracranial process.

2.  Few scattered foci of high signal intensity distributed in the subcortical
white matter, may represent changes due to small vessel disease.

3.  Unchanged mucosal thickening at the left maxillary sinus, possibly
representing chronic sinusitis, please correlate clinically.

INDICATION:  Multiple myeloma with pneumonia and continued hypoxia, assess for
progression of pneumonia.

TECHNIQUE:  PA and lateral radiographs of the chest.

COMPARISON:  Chest radiographs ___.

FINDINGS:  Lung volumes are decreased which can mimic worsened opacification. 
With that in mind, right basilar peribronchial opacity is increased with
unchanged left lower lobar consolidation.  Minimal if any left pleural
effusion is present.  Remainder of lungs are clear.  The heart is normal in
size with normal cardiomediastinal silhouette.  There is no right pleural
effusion or pneumothorax.

IMPRESSION:  Unchanged left lower lobe pneumonia with interval development of
right basal peribronchial opacification.

HISTORY:  ___ male with multiple myeloma, COPD, worsening pneumonia.

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph one day earlier and CT chest ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT helical acquisition was performed through the chest without
IV contrast.  Axial 5- and 1.25-mm collimation images as well as a series of
reformation images were reviewed.

CT CHEST WITHOUT IV CONTRAST:  There is no axillary or supraclavicular
lymphadenopathy.  No new mediastinal nodes are seen, but several are slightly
increased in size (e.g. 7 mm rightupper paratracheal node; 2:11).  Dense left
coronary artery calcifications, and a two right coronary artery stents are
seen.  Low density of intracardiac contents indicates anemia.

Diffuse emphysema is unchanged.  There is no pleural or pericardial effusion. 
The trachea and bronchi are patent to the subsegmental levels.  A previously
seen diffuse infectious process is improved, but a new left lower lobe
peripheral 3.8 cm consolidation and additional areas of inferior nodular
___ opacity suggests acute pneumonia (3:41).  A new 9 mm lingular
nodule may also be infectious (4:118) but followup CT in 8 - 12 weeks is
recommended.  A right middle lobe minor fissural nodule measures 5 mm which is
increased since ___ (4:139).  On the major fissure, an area of focal
thickening spans 8 mm, also increased (4:178).  Both lung bases demonstrate
slight increase in degree of dependent atelectasis.  

Right ninth and left eighth rib fractures appear chronic (2:57).  There is a
distal right clavicle chronic fracture.  There are diffuse changes of myeloma
throughout the bony thorax, especiall in the ribs, which appear mottled.  The
visualized upper abdomen is unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:

1.  Left lower lobe pneumonia, likely typical/bacterial, but aspergillosis
infection, and less likely PTLD or COP are considerations.

2.  New ___ m lingular nodule, may also be infectious though followup CT in 8 -
12 weeks is recommended.

3.  Increase in right middle lobe minor fissural nodule, now 5 mm.

4.  Anemia.

5.  Slight increase in size of borderline mediastinal nodes.

6.  Chronic rib/clavicle fractures, underlying bony myeloma changes.

EXAM:  MRI of the cervical and thoracic spine.

CLINICAL INFORMATION:  Patient with history of multiple myeloma, worsening
neck and back pain, evaluate for fractures.

TECHNIQUE:  T1, T2 and inversion recovery sagittal and T2 axial images of
cervical and thoracic spine were acquired.

FINDINGS:  At the craniocervical junction and C2-3 mild degenerative changes
seen.  At C3-4 there is disc bulging and posterior ridging resulting in
moderate spinal stenosis with mild extrinsic indentation on the spinal cord. 
There is moderate-to-severe left-sided and mild right-sided foraminal
narrowing.

At C4-5 disc bulging and right-sided disc osteophyte severely narrows the
right foramen with moderate narrowing of the left foramen.

At C5-6 there is disc bulging identified with moderate right-sided and mild
left-sided foraminal narrowing.  At C6-7 and C7-T1 mild degenerative changes
are identified.

From T1-T6 level there is no compression fracture or marrow edema identified. 
Mild disc degenerative change is seen.  At T7 and T8 level there is mild
anterior wedging of the vertebral bodies seen.  There is no definite increased
signal seen within the vertebral bodies on inversion recovery images
indicative of late subacute chronic compressions.  There is no abnormal signal
seen within the spinal cord.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Changes of cervical spondylosis with moderate spinal stenosis at C3-4
level with mild extrinsic indentation on the spinal cord.
2.  Late subacute to chronic-appearing compressions of T7 and T8 vertebral
bodies.  No acute compression fracture seen.
3.  No evidence of focal bony abnormalities.  Mild heterogeneity of the bone
marrow signal seen which could be secondary to osteopenia.

INDICATION:  New right PICC, assess for placement.

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph ___.

FINDINGS:  New right-sided PICC line is seen ending at the mid SVC.  Decrease

no pleural effusion or pneumothorax.  Cardiomediastinal silhouette is
unchanged.

IMPRESSION:
1.  New right PICC ending in the mid SVC.
2.  Decrease in left basal consolidation suggesting clearing of pneumonia.
